prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official Node.js release documentation, here is the information on the lifecycle of its LTS releases.

The Node.js project maintains a predictable release schedule with defined periods for Active LTS and Maintenance LTS. The key detail is that each major release line enters Active LTS for 12 months and then Maintenance LTS for 18 months, for a total LTS lifespan of 30 months from its entry into LTS.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-schedule | QUOTE: "Active LTS for a major release line is 12 months" | CLAIM: The Active LTS phase lasts for 12 months.
SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-schedule | QUOTE: "Maintenance LTS for a major release line is 18 months" | CLAIM: The Maintenance LTS phase lasts for 18 months.
SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-schedule | QUOTE: "A major release line enters LTS status... for a total LTS lifespan of 30 months." | CLAIM: The total LTS period (Active + Maintenance) for a release is 30 months.
